News.title: Thousands of migrants line up for citizenship documents after socialist Spain opens its doors to up to 1.3MILLION
News.content:
RUBBER STAMP-EDE Thousands of migrants line up for citizenship documents after socialist Spain opens its doors to up to 1.3MILLION

HUGE queues have formed in cities across Spain as the socialist-led country approved plans to give legal status to hundreds of thousands of migrants.

Migrants waited for hours in enormous lines, with some even staying overnight, desperate to get their paperwork rubber-stamped.





The scheme gives legal status to all foreign nationals who can prove they do not have a criminal record, entered Spain before the start of 2026 and have lived in the country for at least five months at the time they apply.

Online applications opened last Thursday after the programme was approved by PM Pedro Sánchez’s socialist government.

Now hopeful migrants are waiting at more than 400 locations across the country for in-person appointments.

Seville’s town hall considered closing early due to the huge numbers of people waiting, according to Diario de Sevilla.



One Columbian migrant waiting in Barcelona told El Periodico that he had arrived at “around 10 or 11pm last night so we wouldn’t be left out” and had been waiting around 15 hours.

A Honduran migrant told the paper he had slept on the floor to save his place in the queue, adding: “A very large group of people almost trampled me… We risked our lives, but it will be worth it.”

Successful applicants will be allowed to work legally and receive a one-year residency permit, with the option to extend.

The Spanish government first estimated that this would give legal status to around 500,000 people.



But analysis by the National Centre for Immigration and Borders (CNIF) later suggested that between 750,000 and one million illegal migrants currently in Spain would apply for legal status.

And a further 250,000 to 350,000 asylum seekers may also seek legal status.

Experts forecast “secondary movements” of up to 250,000 illegal migrants per year from other Schengen-area countries into Spain over the medium to long term.

It means a total of up to 1.3million people could now be granted legal status through the scheme.

Thousands of migrants descended on their consulates across Spain last week to get documents to prove they do not have a criminal record.



A huge queue formed outside the Pakistani consulate in January, before the plan had been fully confirmed.

Tech mogul Elon Musk then got into a row with left wing Socialist Sánchez over the policy.

Musk’s fracas with the PM started when the X-owner reposted a tweet that claimed PM Sanchez was “dropping the mask” with blatant “electoral engineering” “under the guise of defeating the far-right”.



Musk shared the X post and added “wow”, enraging Sanchez, who hit back.

The Spanish PM replied: “Mars can wait. Humanity can’t.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It was a jab at Musk’s Starship project, which is trying to create the most powerful rocket in the world as part of SpaceX’s bid to take humanity to Mars.

Socialist Sánchez argues that his plan is needed to combat workforce shortages, and boost his country’s ailing economy.

News.title: Moment Reform MP is KICKED OUT of Commons after branding Keir Starmer a liar
News.content:
A REFORM MP was booted out of the Commons today for accusing Sir Keir Starmer of “lying”.

Lee Anderson blasted the PM’s defence of appointing Peter Mandelsonas US Ambassador, warning “no one believes him”.





In a question to Sir Keir, the outspoken politician blasted: “The public doesn’t believe him, the MPs on this side of the House don’t believe him, his own gullible backbenchers don’t believe him, so does the PM agree with me he’s been lying?”

Mr Anderson was told off by Commons Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle.

Under archaic parliamentary rules MPs cannot be accused of lying.

But after being told to withdraw his comment, Mr Anderson responded: “I will not withdraw – that man couldn’t lie straight in bed.”

He was subsequently ordered to leave the chamber.

It comes as Sir Keir today admitted it was “staggering” he was never told Mandelson had failed top-level security vetting – as he scrambled to contain the deepening row.

The PM insisted officials granted Mandelson clearance despite a formal recommendation it should be denied and did not tell him, the Foreign Secretary or even the Cabinet Secretary.



He also confirmed the Foreign Office’s power to overrule vetting decisions has now been suspended, and a fresh probe into the system launched.

The crisis erupted after The Guardian revealed Mandelson had failed security vetting last week, triggering the sacking of senior official Sir Olly Robbins.

Addressing the Commons today, Sir Keir pointed the finger at Foreign Office officials, accusing them of failing to “sensibly flag” the recommendation before Mandelson took up the Washington role.

The PM said there was “no law” preventing civil servants from warning ministers about vetting concerns while protecting sensitive details.

He told MPs: “The recommendation in the Peter Mandelson case could and should have been shared with me before he took up his post,..



“If I had known before he took up his post, the UKSV (United Kingdom Security Vetting ) recommendation was that developed vetting clearance would be denied, I would not have gone ahead with the appointment.”

The PM said he found it “astonishing” and “staggering” that not only was he kept in the dark — but the then Cabinet Secretary was also not told during a formal review of the appointment.

He went on: “I know many members across the House will find these facts to be incredible, and to that I can only say that they are right. It beggars belief that throughout the whole timeline of events, officials in the Foreign Office saw fit to withhold this information from the most senior ministers in our system of government.

“That is not how the vast majority of people in this country expects politics, government or accountability to work, and I do not think it’s how most public servants think it should work.”

The row comes after Sir Keir insisted three times at PMQs — just a day before Mandelson was sacked — that “full due process” had been followed.



Ministers are expected to correct the record swiftly if they mislead Parliament, even inadvertently.

But the Tories say the PM has failed to do so, despite being told last Tuesday that Mandelson had failed vetting.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch accused the Prime Minister of breaching the ministerial code by waiting nearly a week to come to the Commons.

She said: “His reputation is at stake. Everyone is watching. It is finally time for the truth.”

Arguing that Sir Keir Starmer inadvertently misled the House, she said: “I will remind him that, under the ministerial code, he has a duty to correct the record at the earliest opportunity.



“The Prime Minister says he only found out on Tuesday that Peter Mandelson failed the security vetting. The earliest opportunity to correct the record was Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday, almost a week ago. This is a breach of the ministerial code.”

Responding, Sir Keir said: “When I found out what had happened on Tuesday evening last, I wanted to have answers to the question: who made the decision to recommend to give clearance on developed vetting, contrary to the advice, why that was done and who knew about it, so I could provide the information to the House.

“That is the exercise that’s been conducted since Tuesday evening and today, so that I could come here today to give the full account to the House, which I’ve just set out.”

Fresh documents published hours before today’s Commons statement also show Sir Keir was warned to wait for checks to be completed before confirming the appointment.

Ahead of hiring the Labour peer, then Cabinet Secretary Lord Case told the PM: “You should give us the name of the person you would like to appoint and we will develop a plan for them to acquire the necessary security clearances and do due diligence on any potential Conflicts of Interest or other issues of which you should be aware before confirming your choice.”



It raises questions over why Sir Keir did not wait for the vetting to be done before announcing Lord Mandelson to the public as his man in Washington.

The axed Foreign Office chief will give his own evidence to MPs tomorrow to set out his version of events.

Sir Keir is under huge pressure over a slew of policy U-turns, dismal poll ratings and calls for him to resign — but allies have told wannabe leadership challengers to put the country first.

Senior government sources have claimed it was Mandelson’s foreign links that led to a recommendation against his appointment, rather than his friendship with paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein.

Mandelson was sacked last year less than 12 months after he was appointed when details emerged of his ties with Epstein.



It was revealed last week that he was not granted developed vetting status during the appointment process but this was overturned by Sir Olly, who did not tell No 10.

However, No 10 believes he had the opportunity to raise the report on four different occasions.

It says it could have been disclosed when he saw the advice or when Mandelson was sacked.

Insiders revealed he could have also raised the issue when the Government was forced to release material on the appointment and also when ministers said they would review security vetting last month.

But he was not stopped by law from “sensibly flagging” recommendations from the vetting body regarding Mandelson’s appointment, a Government document reveals.



Paperwork released last night says there is “nothing in the guidance” that prevented details being shared in the Mandelson scenario.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The law states that civil servants make decisions on vetting and clearance but they can raise recommendations to ministers to make judgments, appointments or even explaining matters to Parliament.

It states that this could have been done in a “proportionate and necessary way” if in line with the appropriate steps.

News.title: I visited US fat capital ‘designed to make you obese’… where 28st locals wear size XXXXXL & scoff 10k calories a DAY
News.content:
TWENTY-EIGHT stone Rudy Mendiola wipes his mouth after his daily, 5,000-calorie junk food meal and tells me: “This is the danger zone.”

Welcome to America’s fat ­capital, where the air is choked with stale oil from endless fast food restaurants and stores are stacked with giant clothes for supersized shoppers.



I’m in McAllen, southern Texas, a town with an outsized reputation as the fattest place in America, a ­dubious honour it has held for the past three years.



Half of the 150,000 population in this calorie-laden outpost is obese, and another third is overweight.

Uber driver Rudy, 48, tells me it’s “normal” to be fat in McAllen, and he is right. Everywhere you look, there are oversized people.

It is little wonder, given it is a place where fizzy drinks are cheaper than water at a dollar each, residents typically munch through 10,000 calories a day, and food is described by locals as a dangerous “drug”.

The town is home to 500 fast food restaurants — that is one per every 300 people.

In one of the popular all-you-can-eat Chinese buffets, people are so addicted they cannot even wait to take a table before tucking in — a warning sign on the wall tells diners to step away from the food counters before delving into their brimming plates.



Within one minute of driving into McAllen, I was confronted with ten giant neon signs displaying $5 (£3.50) pizzas, $6 burger ­combos and $4 tacos.

The city also seems designed to ­fatten people. It is nigh on impossible to walk. There are no pavements alongside 55mph-limit roads, no cycle lanes, only a handful of gyms — and everything is a drive-thru.

Motorised scooters that you can rent via a mobile phone app for the day to save waddling around are in shopping malls and supermarkets.

Rudy, who is looking for love but bemoans that his last date was a catfish as she was “too big”, says: “It’s normal to be overweight here, so ­people don’t lose it as no one judges.”

He adds: “I know I eat more than I’m supposed to, and I eat the wrong foods.



“I don’t get long breaks and have to grab fast food. That’s Whata- burger, Chinese food or chicken strips.

“I can sometimes only eat one meal a day, but it could be in excess of 5,000 calories. Coffees and drinks rack up more calories.

“I’ve had two knee surgeries, as the weight I have on my body means three times as much stress for my knees.

“I have arthritis and chronic kidney stones. It’s a danger zone here.”

Even teenagers in the city recognise that the locals are on the front line of an obesity crisis which is destroying the nation’s health.



And with worrying echoes of the US fentanyl crisis, where whole towns became awash with abuse of the prescription painkiller, Bella Lopez, 18, said: “The food here has become almost a drug.”

It’s cheaper to buy takeout food than make it at home. Luis

At the local Walmart, where they sell XXXXXL clothes, I meet Rose, 31, who weighs more than 25st, and her husband Luis, 26, weighing 26st, who have a starkly worded warning: “You will get fat if you move here.”

They also explain how the heavy influence of Texas’s Mexican immigrant population has supercharged the ­obesity problem.

Luis, who is of Mexican origin, is out shopping with their three children. He says: “There’s a lot of ­Mexican culture here, which is all about food, and that meets Texan culture, where the mantra is everything is bigger.

“The portion sizes become way ­bigger, even in supermarkets.”



Luis holds up a three-litre bottle of Diet Coke — special to the area — as an example.

“It’s cheaper to buy takeout food than make it at home,” he explains.

“Even with the kids, we needed to do the food shopping and the fastest thing to get them was a basket of fries and chicken tenders, which were being sold at the front of the store.”

He admits the family’s favourite snack is Chicharron, a popular dish of fried pork belly or pork rinds, with a Mexican cola, which uses cane sugar instead of corn syrup, but adds: “We have been trying hard to lose weight.



“We gained during Covid because pre-Covid I was 210lbs (15st) and went up to 390lbs (27st 12lbs). Now I’m down to 360lbs (25st 10lbs).

“We are desperate to get healthy.”



The same can’t be said for the lady in front of us, who is buying 24 cans of cola, two bags of pork scratchings, a bag of Oreo cookies, cookie dough biscuits and cheese crackers.

There is not a vegetable in sight.

‘Snacking is a big thing’

Laura Landeros, 61, who has to use a mobility scooter to get around the store due to her weight, proudly tells us: “Snacking is a big thing here. If you don’t have snacks, you’re boring.

“My favourites are these pork cracklings and Doritos. I make a ­guacamole cream sauce for them.

“I’m a hardcore Coca-Cola fan, too, but my favourite is Dr Pepper, the cherry flavour.”



Outside the supermarket, dozens of vending machines offer dollar (70p) fizzy drinks.

And the local petrol ­station, Stripes, sells a 1.5litre cup of pop of your choice, called the Big Gulp, for just a dollar, while a 500ml bottle of water is $3 (£2.20).

As local demand is so high, Coca-Cola operates a massive distribution centre on the edge of town.

Dietitian Brandon Harper, who runs Harper/Cook nutrition with his wife, says residents here can easily ­consume more than 10,000 calories a day and eat all three meals out.

He said: “We have a really big influence from Mexican culture.



“A quesadilla would normally ­consist of two tortillas with a bit of chicken and cheese, but it becomes super-sized.

“It becomes two massive tortillas and mountains of cheese with excess protein and added avocado and tortilla chips. It becomes huge.

“And everyone here lives a ­sedentary life.”

There are bed-bound people here who are over 400lbs. Nurse Daniela Delgardo

The Black Bear diner is home to a 1,710-calorie breakfast named The Volcano — and your insides could erupt with the three sweet cream pancakes, two sausages, two slices of thick-cut bacon and maple syrup.

I tried the meal, and after just three bites, I felt sick to the point I was heaving from the overload of sugar.



It made me feel so ill that I couldn’t eat a thing for the rest of the day. I was bent over double on the side of the restaurant, praying that I would vomit.

Texan fast food franchise Whataburger, with its distinctive orange ‘W’ logo, is a beacon for locals, and its triple cheeseburger combo meal is one of the most popular items.

It comes in at 2,220 calories — more than a woman’s recommended daily limit of 2,000 calories.

One hefty man queuing for his cheeseburger said: “Loads of people here eat fast food for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Why not? It’s tasty and cheap.”

He adds that the town had to open more branches of the burger chain because the queues were so big.



There are now six in a tiny radius.

Nurse Daniela Delgardo, who works on the cardiac unit at the hospital in the region, told The Sun: “We see a lot of high blood pressure and ­diabetes, which is life-threatening.

‘Can’t fit through my door’

“There are bed-bound people here who are over 400lbs (28st 8lbs).

“There’s a lot of access to fast food, which contains sodium and artificial ingredients.

“We have a lot of people here who are also on government-issued food stamps because they are on a low income and have a low education, so they don’t know how to read ingredients and what calories mean.



“They then get hooked on the sugar and additives, so it’s a domino effect.

“There’s a link between the two socio-economically.”

One 5ft 8in local, who weighs at least 43st, lives his life entirely in his bed because of his extreme weight.

The man, who has asked for his identity to be concealed, says he used to have substance abuse issues. After quitting drugs, he replaced his fix with food.

He explains: “I would eat three McChicken burgers, a Big Mac combo, cookies, 20-piece nuggets with the sauce, large fries, and, after that, I would eat three more meals.



“I would get full, but my mind would tell me I was still hungry.

“I gained 200lbs (14st 4lbs) in nine months, and now I can’t even fit through my door.”



Even a visit to a petrol station in McAllen sees locals filling up more than their cars.

The restaurants on the forecourt sell some of the most calorific meals in the city, with a simple dish of chicken and rice coming in at just under 2,000 calories.

While more than 40 per cent of US adults are obese, and nearly three in four are considered overweight or obese, the US government is focusing on improving healthy food access, increasing taxes on sugary drinks and providing FDA-approved medication.

But I am told fat jabs like Ozempic and Mounjaro, which have surged in the US, with 12 per cent of adults on them, are not considered in McAllen.

BIG LOSERS HERE are three US cities that tackled their obesity crisis in interesting ways: OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA IN one of the nation’s most obese cities, mayor Mick Cornett led a campaign in 2008 for locals to lose a collective one million pounds in weight, bringing in initiatives to build more pavements and parks plus better public transport. They met the goal by 2012. MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA CONSISTENTLY ranked as one of the healthiest cities in America, Minneapolis curbs obesity by banning new restaurant drive-thrus and strives to make the city more walkable. HUNTINGTON, WEST VIRGINIA DUBBED “America’s fattest city” in 2008, it has reduced its obesity rate from 44 per cent to roughly 32 per cent as of 2019. While still above the national average, the city achieved this through community-wide health initiatives and lifestyle changes.

This is due to a mix of locals not being able to afford them — more than 20 per cent of residents live in poverty, and one in four households is on benefits — as well as citizens ­simply feeling that “fat is the norm”.



It is a chilling glimpse into how ­serious the UK’s obesity crisis could become.

Almost 30 per cent of adults in England are living with obesity, with 66 per cent classified as overweight or obese, creating a major public health crisis.

McAllen bartender Sam, who weighs 17st, is trying to lose weight by ditching junk food, but says the real draw is the all-you-can-eat ­Chinese buffets.

He says: “We love it here. It’s only $12.99 (£9.50) for as much as you want. They even have signs to say, ‘Please do not eat in the buffet area’ because people are so addicted.”

Two teenage pals, Clarissa Garcia, 18, and Evely Soto, 19, say they are already on a dangerous trajectory.



They tell me: “We’ve tried to lose weight, but it’s so hard. It’s harder here than anywhere else.”

News.title: Jaw-dropping moment tourist-packed hot air balloon performs emergency landing in homeowners’ GARDEN: ‘Hi everybody!’
News.content:
THIS is the incredible moment a packed hot air balloon is forced to make an early morning emergency landing in a couple’s back garden.

The giant blue and yellow hot air balloon plopped down to Earth after soaring across California skies on Saturday morning, much to the shock of homeowners Hunter and Jenna Perrin.





The Temecula couple were watching TV around 8.30am when a frantic knocking alarmed them.

Their neighbour was at their door and told them a hot air balloon had just landed in their backyard.

“I open the sliding glass door, and there’s a basket full of thirteen people in my backyard!” Hunter told Eyewitness News.



“Hi everyone!” Hunter can be heard shouting to the drop-ins and he laughs at the absurdity of the situation.

The tourist balloon was packed with 13 people who were equally surprised to have landed in the suburban garden.

A passenger can be heard shouting: “We’re in someone’s backyard! Bend your knees!”

The wind had completely died down which forced the pilot to make an emergency landing.



He was reportedly aiming for the street but didn’t have enough fuel to make it safely down in time.

Instead, he chose the Perrin’s backyard, narrowly avoiding fences and trees.

Hunter said: “The pilot, he was masterful. He got it right down inside, like directly into the backyard, where there was nothing. The balloon didn’t catch on anything. No one was injured.”

“He kind of plopped straight down and was moving very slowly.”

Jenna said she had heard something strange moments before seeing the balloon.



“And I run to the backyard, and there’s a whole group of people that are just waving at me,” she said.

“And I’m like, ‘Oh my God. So the sound I heard was the flames?!’ And I’m like… hi!'”



Passenger Brianna Avalos was celebrating her 10 year anniversary with her husband when the balloon had to come back down to Earth a little earlier than planned.

“[The pilot] was trying to get us to the street, but we couldn’t get to the street in time, so we landed in the people’s backyard safe and sound, like no one’s hurt, everyone’s great. He was an amazing pilot!” Avalos said.

Neighbours had gathered on the street when they had noticed how close the balloon was to their rooftops and had tried to bring the balloon down to safety.

More propane was eventually delivered and the balloon was reignited with just the pilot inside.

He “jumed” the house and landed it back onto the street.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We’re just happy that everyone was safe,” Hunter said. “It’s just such a whimsical story.”

News.title: Can you spot what’s off about these elephants? Eagle-eyed tourists make shocking discovery at Chinese theme park
News.content:
TOURISTS have make shocking discovery at a theme park in China after eagle-eyed viewers noticed something unusual about two “elephants”.

Footage shared online shows the tuskers appearing on stage at an amusement park in central China.





But incredulous viewers noticed something bizarre – a pair of human ankles poking out from beneath a bulky animal costume.

The “elephants” were part of a storytelling segment at Wansui Mountain Martial Arts City in Kaifeng.

The elaborate show also included a molten iron fireworks performance.



Some said they had watched the performance multiple times and had always assumed the elephants were genuine.

Others praised the park for using performers instead of real animals because it was more ethical.

Staff from the centre cleared up the confusion on April 15 and confirmed that they did not keep elephants at their park.

They explained that the animals seen in the show are props operated by between two and four staff members working together inside the costume.



The performance was part of a wider immersive experience at the park, which combines Song Dynasty culture with martial arts-themed entertainment, live shows, and traditional folk acts.

While some visitors felt misled, others said the revelation made the show more interesting.

It follows a hilarious discovery made by zoo visitors at Guangyuan park in China.

Tourists sensed something strange when the zoo’s so-called “pandas” started barking.

The furry fiends were in fact dogs painted black and white to look like the famous cuddly bears.



Zoo visitors demanded their money back after being deceived by the duplicitous park, which claimed to house “rare and exotic animals”.

In Japan, zoo staffers paid a bizarre tribute to their lost pandas – by dressing up as the cuddly bears.

Workers donned panda hats in honour of the four endangered pandas that were returned to China.

News.title: Teacher ‘sexually assaulted baby boy he was adopting then filmed him as he lay dying on bed with horror injuries’
News.content:
BABY 'MURDER' Teacher ‘sexually assaulted baby boy he was adopting then filmed him as he lay dying on bed with horror injuries’

A TEACHER sexually assaulted a baby boy he was adopting then filmed him as he lay dying on the bed, a murder trial heard today.

Little Preston Davey was allegedly “routinely ill-treated” by Jamie Varley, who took indecent pictures and videos of the 13-month-old.





Jurors heard Varley, 37, filmed Preston being spun so fast in a saucer at a play area on one occasion that his eyes appeared to go in different directions.

He also allegedly forced the tot to stay awake and filmed himself deliberately startling the baby.

Varley and his partner John McGowan-Fazakerley are both accused of sexually assaulting Preston, who they were in the process of formally adopting.

Preston Crown Court heard McGowan-Fazakerley, 32, was aware of the psychological and physical abuse Varley was inflicting but allegedly “wilfully neglected to protect Preston”.

The youngster was rushed to hospital on three occasions before his death suffering from breathing difficulties, seizures, a nose bleed and a fracture to his arm.

Staff noticed facial bruising but it was explained sufficiently by the defendants and he recovered quickly, the court heard.

In July last year, Varley allegedly caused Preston serious internal injuries after he sexually assaulted at home in Blackpool, Lancashire.



Jurors heard he then failed to call for help and instead caused the tot further harm.

A video later found on his phone showed Preston lying on a bed in respiratory arrest with his lips blue, it was said.

The court heard McGowan-Fazackerly had been at work and Varley was the sole carer for Preston that day.

He was eventually rushed to Blackpool Victoria Hospital where he died from an acute obstruction of his upper airway.

Jurors were told this was caused either a smothering with a hand or fabric or the insertion of an object into Preston’s mouth.



Prosecutor Peter Wright KC said: “As terrible as it is, this was not the result of some dreadful yet unforeseen accident or natural phenomenon.

“The evidence gathered during the investigation into his untimely death revealed a much more sinister pathology.

“We say the evidence demonstrates that he was murdered by one of the people entrusted with his well-being, one of his proposed adoptive parents, Jamie Varley.

“But this was not the only tragedy to befall him when in the care of these defendants. In the final moments of his short life, he was routinely ill treated, sexually abused and physically assaulted.”

Jurors heard Varley recorded some of the alleged abuse on his phone and shared it with McGowan-Fazackerly.



Mr Wright said this included a video of Preston “slithering and sliding in a bath” for 14 minutes while Varley failed to help him.

The prosecutor continued: “These are not happy snaps of a normal family life . They are indecent images.

“It is not difficult to distinguish between happy snaps and indecent images.”

The court heard Preston was born four weeks early and taken into local authority care at birth.

He lived happily with foster carers for the first nine months of his life while suitable adoptive parents were found.



Both Varley and McGowan-Fazackerly were both in a stable relationship and were keen to adopt a child, jurors were told.

They went through the adoption process from December 2021 to March 2022 and had been vetted well before Preston was born.

The couple visited Preston in February 2023 and he was assessed as “fit and healthy” with no underlying conditions, the court heard.

In March 2023, a proposed adoption was approved by the panel and he went to live with Varley and McGowan-Fazackerly the following month.

Varley denies murder, sexual assault of a child under 13, inflicting grievous bodily harm, five counts of child cruelty and further counts of making, taking and distributing indecent images.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

McGowan-Fazakerley pleaded not guilty to causing and allowing the death of a child, two counts of child cruelty and sexual assault of a child under 13.

The trial continues.

News.title: Kids will be allowed to wear TRACKSUITS in school under MPs’ plans to make uniform ‘inclusive’
News.content:
SMART CASUAL Kids will be allowed to wear TRACKSUITS in school under MPs’ plans to make uniform ‘inclusive’

PUPILS should be allowed to wear tracksuits and trainers at school to make uniform more inclusive, MPs have proposed.

The relaxation of dress codes across the country will allow children to move more freely at school, according to a new report.





Titled ‘Game On’ and published by the Government’s culture, media and sport committee on Monday, the report claims that the current PE kit used at schools is too restrictive and creates “barriers to activity”.

According to the report, girls are more likely to describe PE as “embarrassing” or “stressful”, whereas boys tend to describe it as “exciting” and “engaging”.

It argues that the uniform change would boost girls’ participation in school life.

“We recommend that the Government issue guidance making clear that schools are expected to adopt PE kit and uniform policies that prioritise comfort, inclusivity and dignity, particularly for girls and pupils with protected characteristics,” the report says.

“The Government should also promote more practical, activity-friendly school uniforms, such as allowing sportswear or trainers as standard, to ensure pupils can move comfortably throughout the day.

“These measures would help reduce barriers to activity, lower costs for families and increase participation, particularly among girls.”

The committee is calling on the Government to include less mainstream sports – such as skateboarding, cheerleading and parkour – in an attempt to diversify the PE curriculum and make it more “fun and inclusive”.

It is also urging the Prime Minister to double Government spending on sport and recreation from 0.3 per cent to 0.6 per cent.



“Evidence shows that a narrow, traditional PE curriculum often alienates pupils who feel less confident or ‘sporty’’ particularly girls and children with Send,” said the committee.

“Broadening the offer to include non-traditional sports, dance and outdoor activities helps make PE more enjoyable and accessible, supporting physical literacy and long-term engagement.”

Dame Caroline Dinenage, the Tory chairman of the committee, said: “We’re a country of sport lovers when it comes to supporting our stars at home and abroad, but there are too many barriers stopping people from getting up and giving it a go themselves at school and clubs in our communities.

“Taking part in sport isn’t just for those aspiring to be the next Joe Root or Lucy Bronze. Everyone deserves the chance to feel the upsides of being more active.

“What we need now is a big effort to ensure everyone is rowing in the same direction to get the nation moving.”



Not everyone views the suggestions enthusiastically, however.

Commenting on the report, one Facebook user wrote: “Ridiculous. A uniform is standard and shows respect for the school and so everyone looks the same.”

Another wrote: “No way. My kids go to a school where there are rich and poor [children]. Uniform levels their backgrounds.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Department for Education spokesman said: “School leaders are responsible for deciding whether to have a school uniform and what it should be, but our guidance is clear that schools should engage with parents and pupils when designing their uniform policy and should consider how comfortable the proposed uniform will be for pupils.

“We know that too many young people remain inactive, which is why our new PE and School Sport Partnerships will target the barriers that hold children back, ensuring more opportunities for those who are less active including girls, pupils from less affluent backgrounds, those from ethnically diverse communities and pupils with Send.”

News.title: Louisiana shooter’s chilling final moments after evil dad gunned down eight children and left carnage across two houses
News.content:
LAST STEPS Louisiana shooter’s chilling final moments after evil dad gunned down eight children and left carnage across two houses

A TWISTED father spent his final hours taking his eldest daughter on a dinner date, then returned home and executed eight of his own children in cold blood before being gunned down by police.

The chilling contrast between the cheerful social media post and the carnage that followed has left a Louisiana city reeling.





Shamar Elkins, 31, unleashed a bloodbath in the early hours of Sunday morning, shooting dead seven children inside a home before an eighth was found dead on the roof, believed to have been trying to escape.

The massacre unfolded across multiple locations in Shreveport, with bullets fired in at least two residences.

Eight children aged between three and 11 were killed, most shot “execution style,” police said.

Two women, believed to be the mothers of his children, were also shot and wounded in the attack.

Elkins’ wife, Shaneiqua Pugh, was shot in the face and left fighting for her life.



A second woman, thought to be his girlfriend, was wounded at a nearby home.

The rampage is believed to have been sparked by a bitter relationship breakdown, with the couple heading for divorce.

Just hours before the killings, Elkins had posted a smiling photo with his oldest daughter after taking her out to eat, writing that he’d taken her on a “lil 1 on 1 date.”

Days earlier, he had shared a beaming family photo with all seven of his children after taking them to church for Easter, calling it “a blessed day.”

But behind the wholesome posts, those close to him say Elkins had been spiraling for weeks.



On Easter Sunday, the same day he posed with his kids at church, he broke down in tears during a phone call with his mother and stepfather, confessing he was drowning in dark thoughts and wanted to end his life.

His stepfather Marcus Jackson recalled the haunting exchange, saying he urged Elkins to fight through it.

“Then I remember him telling me: ‘Some people don’t come back from their demons,'” Jackson said.

During the call, the children could be heard playing in the background, unaware of what was coming.

Elkins hung up after promising to pass on greetings from their grandparents.



Days later, he killed them.

Earlier this month he had also posted a prayer online begging God to “help me guard my mind and my emotions… when depression tries to settle in, when anger rises.”

After the shootings on the 300 block of West 79th Street, Elkins fled the scene, carjacked a vehicle, and led officers on a high-speed chase.

He drove a quarter-mile to Harrison Street before fleeing to a third location in Bossier Parish, where officers shot and killed him on Brompton Lane.

Shreveport Police Chief Wayne Smith said he was stunned by the scale of the carnage, which unfolded between 5 am and 6 am.



“I just don’t know what to say, my heart is just taken aback,” Smith said.

“I cannot begin to imagine how such an event could occur.”

Mayor Tom Arceneaux called it “maybe the worst tragic situation we’ve ever had.”

Elkins, a UPS worker and former Louisiana Army National Guard soldier who served from 2013 to 2020, was known to police from a 2019 firearms case.

However, authorities said they were unaware of any prior domestic violence issues.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The victims were identified as Jayla Elkins, 3; Shayla Elkins, 5; Kayla Pugh, 6; Sariahh Snow, 11; Khedarrion Snow, 6; and Braylon Snow, 5.

The investigation has been handed to the Louisiana State Police as the crime scene crosses parish boundaries.

News.title: Lee Anderson kicked out of Commons for calling Keir Starmer a liar in Mandelson debate
News.content:
Lee Anderson kicked out of Commons for calling Keir Starmer a liar in Mandelson debate

Reform UK MP Lee Anderson has been kicked out of the Commons after accusing Keir Starmer of lying - it is against the rules to accuse other members of lying in the Commons

View 2 Images Lee Anderson has been kicked out of the Commons (Image: Sky News)

Lee Anderson has been kicked out of the Commons after accusing Keir Starmer of lying in a debate in the Commons.

‌



The Reform UK MP was ticked off by Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle after suggesting the PM was lying about what he knew about Peter Mandelson's vetting. It came as Mr Starmer vented his fury at Foreign Office officials for being kept in the dark over the scandal.

‌



In a tense debate in the chamber, the Tory turncoat told Mr Starmer: "The problem the Prime Minister's got is no one believes him. The public don't believe him, the MPs on this side of the House don't believe him, his own gullible backbenchers don't believe him. So does the Prime Minister agree with me? He's been lying."

‌



Sir Lindsay stepped in: "We don't use those words. And I'm sure the member will withdraw it." Mr Anderson responded: "Mr Speaker, I have the greatest respect for you and your office. But I will not withdraw. That man couldn't lie straight in bed."

Sir Lindsay replied: “Mr Anderson, you’ll have to leave.”

Keir Starmer watch LIVE: PM faces Parliament over Peter Mandelson vetting scandal READ MORE :

View 2 Images The Reform UK MP was ticked off by Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle (above) (Image: Sky News)

‌



Under parliamentary procedure, MPs are not allowed to accuse other members of lying - and they must withdraw any such comment.

During a debate lasting more than an hour, the Prime Minister scrambled to contain the fallout from the row after it emerged last week Lord Mandelson failed security vetting - yet was still appointed Britain's Ambassador to the US.

The PM told the chamber this afternoon that it "beggars belief" he wasn't told Lord Mandelson failed vetting. Mr Starmer has long come under pressure over his decision to appoint the Labour grandee, who had known links to disgraced paedophile Jeffrey Epstein.

‌



In a high-stakes Commons showdown, Mr Starmer insisted he would have cancelled Lord Mandelson's appointment as the UK's top diplomat in Washington had he known the full facts. Launching a scathing attack on the Foreign Office - days after sacking the top official Sir Olly Robbins at the department - he said there was a "deliberate decision" taken repeatedly not to inform him.

Mr Stamer told MPs: "I know many members across the House will find these facts to be incredible, and to that I can only say that they are right. It beggars belief throughout the whole timeline of events, officials in the Foreign Office saw fit to withhold this information from the most senior ministers in our system of government. That is not how the vast majority of people in this country expects politics, government or accountability to work, and I do not think it’s how most public servants think it should work.”

The PM's statement comes as Sir Olly, the former head of the Foreign Office, prepares to face MPs tomorrow morning after being sacked by Mr Starmer on Thursday. Speaking earlier, a close friend of Sir Olly said he was "heartbroken".

Article continues below

UN official Tom Fletcher said: "I've known Olly well for a long time - this is a guy who has public service and integrity stitched into his DNA in a way I haven't seen in any other single individual. And I've worked with so many people inside governments. He's had an utterly rough few days and he's a pretty strong kind of character, but I think he's heartbroken."

News.title: 'I warned police about serial sex attacker before Beast of Birkenhead murder'
News.content:
'I warned police about serial sex attacker before Beast of Birkenhead murder'

Peter Sullivan was wrongfully convicted for the killing of Diane Sindall and spent 38 years in prison for a crime he did not commit. Now an ex-Merseyside Police officer claims Diane Sindall may have been victim of a serial sex attacker

View 5 Images Diane Sindall (Image: PA)

An ex-cop warned of a spate of sex attacks before the brutal ' Beast of Birkenhead ' murder. Peter Sullivan was wrongfully convicted for the killing of Diane Sindall and spent 38 years in prison for a crime he did not commit.

‌



Ms Sindall finished her shift at the Wellington pub just before midnight on August 1, 1986 when her blue van ran out of petrol. She began walking along Borough Road in Birkenhead and the next day was found in an alley, stripped half naked and beaten to death.

‌



Sullivan, now 68, was convicted of her murder in 1987. But modern forensic science showed that the killer's DNA found on Sindall's body did not match Sullivan's and he was released last May.

‌



Now an ex-Merseyside Police officer claims two senior detectives told him not to investigate despite his voicing concerns in the case, now subject of a cold case review.

The officer saw "a pattern of attacks in the same area with a similar modus operandi suggesting it was one attacker" shortly before Diane's murder in 1986. He said: "The more I looked at it, the more concerned I became as the pattern suggested escalation - both in frequency and violence - and in my view it was moving towards something far more serious."

His worst fears became a reality when Diane Sindall was brutally murdered just days after he raised the alarm.

‌



Merseyside Police said there was currently no evidence linking Ms Sindall's murder to the other offences. Ms Sindall's partially clothed body was found by a dogwalker in an alley off Borough Road on August 2, 1986.

View 5 Images Peter Sullivan was wrongfully convicted of Diane Sindall's murder (Image: PA)

The officer, who requested anonymity, requested case files for similar offences in the area with a comparable modus operandi He discussed the concerns he had raised for a BBC podcast 'Crime Next Door: The Beast of Birkenhead'. He first encountered the cases after being asked to investigate a sexual assault on Borough Road in July 1986. "Even at first glance, I was struck by the seriousness of the assaults and rapes that had occurred locally," the former officer said. "There was an escalating level of violence in several of them. As an experienced detective familiar with that area, I was shocked not to have been aware of these incidents previously. Given their frequency and severity, I could not understand why a dedicated investigation had not already been initiated."

‌



He recalled one case involving a young woman who was violently assaulted and raped off Borough Road.

"She lost consciousness during the attack and, after regaining it, attempted to crawl to safety," he added. "Tragically, her attacker returned and raped her again. It was a deeply disturbing case. I reported my concerns, explaining that I believed these incidents might be linked and that we could be dealing with a serial offender. Well, from my recollection, I was advised to return the files to Wallasey and not to pursue the matter further."

View 5 Images Diane's blue Fiat van

‌



Ms Sindall was murdered possibly as little as a week later. The murder's savagery led to Mr Sullivan receiving several tabloid nicknames including "The Beast of Birkenhead."

Merseyside Police said: "The current investigation has reviewed relevant offences committed before and after the murder of Diane Sindall. The investigation team has an open mind.

"However, apart from the offence involving a "woman in yellow" who was attacked on Borough Road minutes before Ms Sindall, there is currently no evidence to link the Diane Sindall murder to the other offences."

‌



The spokesperson added two senior officers had since died, "as such, we have no further information in relation to this."

View 5 Images Flowers left at the scene of the murder (Image: Colin Lane/Liverpool Echo)

Earlier this year, the Mirror reported on the 'cold case' team of more than 20 police officers hunting the real 'Beast of Birkenhead'.

‌



Detectives hope to solve the 1986 case using new DNA profiling techniques and issuing a full description of the killer for the first time.

Crimestoppers has a £20,000 reward for information leading to the conviction of the person responsible for Ms Sindall's death.

View 5 Images Det Supt Rachel Wilson is leading a cold case review of the murder of Diane Sindall (Image: Liverpool Echo)

‌



A taxi driver saw Sindall arguing with a man on the main road, thought to be the last time she was seen alive. Police say he was white, 5ft 10in, of slim build and aged in his early twenties, with dark and tidy hair, wearing a dark brown leather jacket and jeans. They believe he was probably the killer. So far 500 men have been eliminated from the inquiry and 43 further samples are being tested.

Officers have taken DNA samples from a person in Leeds, while others have travelled to London, Scotland and as far afield as Australia. Detectives are working through the list to obtain samples for testing. The DNA sample of the killer shows only the Y chromosome, which is passed down almost unchanged from father to son, meaning the samples must be taken from a close male relative. All samples provided to police would only be used as part of this investigation, the officers said, and would be destroyed afterwards.

A plaque in memory of Ms Sindall is located on Borough Road, by the alleyway where she was murdered. It reads: "Diane Sindall, murdered 2.8.1986, because she was a woman. In memory of all our sisters who have been raped and murdered. We will never let it be forgotten."

Article continues below

'Crime Next Door: The Beast of Birkenhead' is available on BBC Sounds.

News.title: Parents want extra security around Jewish schools after new spate of anti-semitic attacks
News.content:
Parents want extra security around Jewish schools after new spate of anti-semitic attacks

Spate of anti-semitic attacks frighten parents who urge authorities for more security at schools

View 5 Images Parents want extra security at Jewish schools after new spate of attacks (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Jewish parents in north west London are asking for increased security at schools in the area after a string of terrifying anti-semitic terror attacks.

The UK’s largest Jewish primary school - Sinai - is barely a mile from the Harrow synagogue which was hit by a firebomb over the weekend. The incident sent shockwaves across the area and several schools are already stepping up patrols to protect their children. Counter terrorism police are investigating the crimes and the Met have specialist teams patrolling outside synagogues, schools and businesses under threat. One parent mum-of-two Melissa Rosen told the Mirror: “I want to see more protection, whether it's police presence or hiring more security.

View 5 Images A police forensic officer works inside a cordon set up near to Kenton United Synagogue in Harrow, north-west London (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

“I feel the authorities have not done enough. I want to see action.” She added: “I am deeply concerned. It's the job of a parent to protect your kids. "We have to be really more vigilant. It is scary not knowing what could happen during the day while they are in school. I am ready to do patrols myself if that would help.

“The catalyst is from the Middle East. But it has become almost trendy to hop on the anti-Semitism bandwagon and make our lives scary.”

View 5 Images Burnt out ambulances removed after anti-semitic attack (Image: Guy Bell/Shutterstock)

Mark Gold, 42, said: “I want more action on security at this school. We need more action, more security. We need higher walls.

“I think the level of threat is increased. I am concerned. I went to a non-Jewish school and we had almost no walls. I want to see more police outside the school, but we don't want to draw undue attention to these sites. If we have loads of police they should rather be mainly plain-clothes.

View 5 Images A police officer outside the Kenton United Synagogue in Harrow, north-west London, after an attempted arson attack (Image: James Manning/PA Wire)

“I think it's problematic all over the world so I do not want to leave the UK. We need to stamp out the antisemitism. I think it's about educating people, and a lot of what is online is really incendiary. People who read this can be easily misled.

"We should remove all Hebrew writing, no matter how small, from the signs around the school. Our logo has some Hebrew on it. We should remain as under the radar as we can."

View 5 Images Security outside Finchley Reform Synagogue in north London after an attempted arson attack (Image: PA)

Article continues below

Another parent, who asked to remain anonymous said: “Governments over the past couple fo decades have allowed political correctness to stop them admitting we have certain groups aiming to do harm to Jewish citizens of the UK. “The authorities must act to get the Muslim community to condemn these things. It's a noisy minority of a minority who are threatening the Jews, and all minorities should stand united against these people.

“I am actually pleased my children go to a Jewish school, as I feel they are not necessarily safe if they were going to a non-Jewish school, where they could face discrimination by indoctrinated fellow-pupils.

“Our police forces across the country have been hollowed out over the last 15 to 20 years, but they are doing their best.”

News.title: Nigel Farage's fresh disaster as Reform 'lottery' winners say they haven't been paid
News.content:
Nigel Farage's fresh disaster as Reform 'lottery' winners say they haven't been paid

Reform UK has issued a statement as residents on a street that won an energy bill competition held by Nigel Farage's party claim they have not recieved any winnings

View 3 Images Nigel Farage and Robert Jenrick with the winners of their energy bill competition

Reform's latest publicity 'stunt' may have just turned into a bigger crisis for Nigel Farage.

‌



The party has come under fire for hosting a controversial energy bill competition where a someone had the chance to win free energy bills for themselves and their entire street for a year.

‌



June, a long-time reform voter from Wigan, turned out to be the winner, but other residents living on her road claim now say they have yet to see a penny.

‌



Mr Farage took to social media to share a video celebrating the win, where he handed over flowers to June and her husband as the party's treasury spokesperson Robert Jenrick held a massive cheque.

View 3 Images The Reform leader congratulated the winners - but others claim they have not been paid

The raffle first faced scrutiny when eagled-eyed social media users spotted a photo of Mr Farage standing behind the couple at a 2019 Brexit event, with some critics suggesting he already knew the winners. In a follow-up post on a local Reform UK page, the winning couple were described as "staunch branch members" of the party.

‌



And now some of the residents living on St Malo Road in Wigan claim they have been 'excluded' from the prize, despite the competition saying every home would receive a letter telling them how to put in a claim.

Angie Ecclestone, 48, told The Telegraph she has not yet received her winnings and said: "I thought to myself I'll believe it when I see it but I didn't realise I had been excluded and that my neighbours had all received a letter and instructions.

"Nigel Farage said the whole street [would be included] but we haven't heard anything. I am in shock. I am the first house on St Malo Road. It's the whole street or not the street. I am mortified."

‌



Another neigbour, Matt Johnson, 53, who was told by his sister he had won, said: "We thought we would hear something from Reform by email or post but at the moment we haven't heard anything. I mean if Reform said at the time it would be the whole street, then we feel like we should be included in that. Our energy bills keep going up and down but they are around £3,500 a year. Having them paid for would make a huge difference."

View 3 Images People noticed the same winner of the competiton was pictured with Farage back in 2021 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Meanwhile Fraser Hayes, 63, said he has not received the winnings, but if he does, he would would give them away. Stating plainly that he isn't fan of the right-wing party, he told the publication: "I have no qualms about depriving Reform of the money and giving to a local kids' charity or maybe even the Labour candidate."

‌



The fallout has transformed a national "energy giveaway" into a potential PR disaster, leaving residents demanding clarity on whether the Reform Party intends to honor its word.

The Telegraph reports that on the street in Greater Manchester, which is divided by St Aubyn's Road, half the residents are yet to recieve a letter.

In response, a Reform UK spokesman told The Mirror: "We posted letters physically through some of the doors on the day but weren't able to deliver to all the addresses on the day. Letters are incoming for the remaining households. We always intended to pay for the whole road, as promised, and will do."

Article continues below

It comes as Manchester police are now reviewing a complaint about the energy bill competition. Mr Farage said last week that he is "not the least bit worried" about claims that his party broke electoral rules with the raffle.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) issued a statement on Friday and said it had received a report about the competition and that officers "are currently reviewing the matter", but did not clarify what the potential offence is.

The Mirror has contacted GMP for further comment.

News.title: Salmon are being 'driven wild' by cocaine pollution, new study finds
News.content:
Salmon are being 'driven wild' by cocaine pollution, new study finds

Drug-crazed salmon are swimming twice as far and spreading out into new areas after being exposed to cocaine pollution from humans, a worrying new study has revealed

View 2 Images A new study has revealed the impact of cocaine pollution on salmon behaviour (file photo) (Image: Jörgen Wiklund / SWNS)

Cocaine pollution from humans is sending salmon into a 'frenzy', a new study has revealed.

‌



Traces of the illegal drug in their natural habitat are altering the way fish interact with their environment, according to scientists, with Juvenile Atlantic salmon swimming greater distances and spreading more widely as a direct result of exposure to narcotics, the findings show.

‌



The study, published in the journal Current Biology, is the first to demonstrate the effects of cocaine contamination on fish behaviour in the wild rather than under laboratory conditions.

‌



To establish how pollutants affected animal movement, an international team of researchers used slow-release chemical implants and acoustic tracking to monitor 105 juvenile Atlantic salmon over eight weeks in Lake Vättern, Sweden.

View 2 Images Cocaine is increasingly being detected in rivers and lakes across the globe (file photo) (Image: GETTY)

Animal testing HORROR as harrowing photos show monkeys, pigs and dogs in crying in pain READ MORE :

The fish were divided into one of three treatment groups: a control group, a group exposed to cocaine, and a group exposed to benzoylecgonine, the primary metabolite of cocaine that is commonly detected in wastewater.

‌



Researchers discovered that fish exposed to benzoylecgonine swam up to 1.9 times further per week than unexposed fish and dispersed up to 12.3 kilometres (7.6 miles) wider across the lake. They noted the changes became increasingly pronounced over time, suggesting that exposure altered how fish occupied space within a complex natural ecosystem.

Study co-author Dr Marcus Michelangeli said the findings were significant because movement played a central role in how animals interacted with their surroundings. He said: "Where fish go determines what they eat, what eats them, and how populations are structured.

"If pollution is changing these patterns, it has the potential to affect ecosystems in ways we are only beginning to understand."

‌



Repeated studies show that cocaine and its metabolites are increasingly being detected in rivers and lakes across the globe, entering waterways primarily through sewage systems that were never designed to fully filter out such compounds. While earlier research suggested cocaine could alter animal behaviour, those studies had been confined to laboratory environments.

This latest study offers the first proof that such effects also occur in the wild, where animals face far more complex environmental conditions. Researchers additionally discovered that the cocaine metabolite benzoylecgonine had an even greater impact on fish movement than cocaine itself.

They describe this as "significant" because risk assessments typically concentrate on the parent compound, despite metabolites being more prevalent in waterways - suggesting current methods may be missing crucial biological effects. However, the team stressed the findings posed no risk to people who eat fish.

‌



They noted that exposure levels reflected those already present in polluted waterways, the compounds break down naturally over time, and the fish studied were juveniles well below legal catch size.

Dr Michelangeli, of Griffith University's Australian Rivers Institute in Brisbane, said the study shed light on a wider concern regarding the types of pollutants making their way into aquatic ecosystems.

He added: "The idea of cocaine affecting fish might seem surprising, but the reality is that pollution is changing these patterns, it has the potential to affect ecosystems in ways we are only beginning to understand. The reality is that wildlife is already being exposed to a vast array of human-derived drugs on a daily basis. The unusual part is not the experiment, it's what's already happening in our waterways."

Article continues below

Dr Michelangeli says future research would seek to establish how widespread the effects are, pinpoint which species face the greatest risk, and examine whether changes in movement patterns result in shifts to fish survival and reproduction.

News.title: England legend helps police catch Ring doorbell harasser after 40-minute chase
News.content:
England legend helps police catch Ring doorbell harasser after 40-minute chase

Former Liverpool and England full-back Stephen Warnock helped catch a man who had been peering through the windows of two women's home in Liverpool - playing a key role in his arrest after weeks of harassment caught on Ring doorbell footage

View 6 Images England legend Stephen Warnock helped apprehend a criminal harrasser (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Stephen Warnock, an England football legend and former Liverpool player, helped police apprehend a man who had spent weeks spying through the windows of two women's home by lying in wait for him.

‌



The 44-year-old defender-turned-pundit waited for Andrew Mulhearn after he was repeatedly filmed on the women's Ring doorbell coming to their front door. Warnock, from Ormskirk, Lancashire, monitored the property with his fiancée, the sister of one of the victims, parking close by at times Mulhearn was expected to appear.

‌



When Mulhearn turned up and realised he might be spotted, he ran off. Warnock gave chase for approximately 40 minutes, trailling the harrasser until police alerted by a 999 call were able to arrest him.

‌



The Liverpool Echo reports that Mulhearn, 30, who lived on the same street as his victims in Mossley Hill, Liverpool was handed a 12-week prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, after admitting two counts of harassment without violence spanning several weeks last summer.

Fake Madeleine McCann stalking trial ends as Karen Spragg grins over not guilty verdict READ MORE :

View 6 Images Warnock, now a pundit, once played for Liverpool and England (Image: BBC)

Warnock told the ECHO his motivation was personal. He said: "I've got two daughters myself, and it is just unfair to allow people to walk around with that power. To have young girls absolutely petrified to walk out of their own home or to even be in their own home is wrong...it is not a nice feeling, and I think the main reason we decided to go to the house was to stop it.

‌



"The police don't have the time and resources to be able to do it. So that was why we said, 'Right, let's go and find out who he is and where he lives', and at least then we could take it to the police, and so they could build a better case.

"I think it's a horrible thing for women to go through." Mulhearn's harassment of the women began in July 2025 when his victims noticed a figure repeatedly appearing at the front of their home via their Ring doorbell camera, initially suspecting it was a burglar casing the property.

View 6 Images Andrew Mulhearn captured on Ring doorbell sentenced for two counts of harassment without violence (Image: Supplied)

‌



However, upon closer inspection, the alarming footage revealed the man turning up at the same time every night and peering through the front window.

After speaking to police, the women were advised to upload the footage and dial 999 should he return. But Warnock told the ECHO he felt compelled to keep watch outside the house himself, "not necessarily to confront him, but at that stage we literally knew nothing about him".

The England international continued: "We sat there for an hour-and-a-half. We set the car alarm off twice, the car started to steam up. It wasn't perfect.

‌



"It was quite humorous if I'm being completely honest. But then around 11pm we saw him walk past the car window and I was like, 'Right, he's here.'" But upon spotting a new camera in the front window of the property, Mulhearn swiftly turned away. Warnock, keen to discover where he lived, exited the car and started following, wearing a hoodie, shorts and cap in an attempt to remain inconspicuous."

View 6 Images The footballing legend trailled the harasser in a bid to discover where he lived (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

"We got to the top of the road, and he walked down a cul-de-sac, and I thought, "Well, I'm not walking down there', Warnock said. "I was quite aware of making sure I didn't get tucked into an area I didn't know. I'm from Ormskirk; I haven't got a clue about the area, so there were elements of fear because you think anything could happen.

‌



"I thought I'll wait because he either lives in one of the houses or he has gone down there because he knows I'm behind him. I crouched down behind a car and he came back out. I continued to follow him and then all of a sudden he picked up his pace and darted away and I lost him."

Warnock spotted a vehicle that had also been tailing Mulhearn and approached the driver. "I went over to the car and said, 'Are you undercover police?'" Warnock continued. "And he was like 'No, I'm the brother who owns the house [where Mulhearn's victims lived].

"I told him I'd lost him but he pointed over and said, 'He's there, you go that way, I'll go here,' so suddenly we had two people on the case. [Mulhearn] kept circling back on himself and I thought he must know we're on him, he knows who I am."

‌



View 6 Images Stephen Warnock during his playing career turning out for Liverpool against Arsenal at Anfield (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

"I thought I have to make myself look different so I thought, 'Right, cap's coming off, hoodie's coming off. How much more can I take off? I'm snookered now.' I was thinking I would grab him and wait for the police to come or get my phone out and at least then I could take a clear picture of him."

However, before he needed to act, an unmarked police vehicle, responding to Warnock's fiancée's call, turned up and detained Mulhearn. "The police officer was like 'we just need to ID him'," Warnock said. "I said, "That's him' and the officer was like, "Who are you?"'. We explained, and he said, 'That's good enough for me'.

‌



"There is a humorous side looking back. It's like a dark comedy, in a serious situation, funny things happen...the police officer was taking our statement and said they had to go to another job. I said 'I'm free if you want'."

Mulhearn was arrested, questioned and ultimately charged. Nevertheless, he initially rejected any wrongdoing, insisting that he had merely been peering through the front window to check if anyone was home so he could use the toilet.

View 6 Images Andrew Mulhearn captured on Ring doorbell sentenced for two counts of harassment without violence (Image: Supplied)

‌



However, Mulhearn formally admitted guilt on Tuesday at Liverpool Magistrates' Court. He was sentenced the same day, with the district judge delivering scathing remarks. Mulhearn was also ordered to complete 25 rehabilitation days and 200 hours of unpaid work.

Most crucially for the victims, he was also issued with a five-year restraining order. When asked why he chose to speak out, Warnock, now a pundit working for the likes of the BBC and BT Sports, explained: "Sometimes you hear of harassment cases, but you don't actually understand the effect it can have on [the victims].

"Speaking to them closely and understanding what they were going through wasn't a nice thing to listen to. I think that's ultimately why I decided to try and step in and do something about it at the very least. It felt very predatory. I just thought if you put yourself in their shoes, how would you feel?

Article continues below

"It is one thing saying to women 'Don't walk around late at night', but you are putting the onus on the woman. And this was like, 'Oh, actually you are in your own home where you should be safe."

Bournemouth have announced Marco Rose will take over as the club’s head coach this summer, succeeding Andoni Iraola.

The German has agreed a three-year deal at the Vitality Stadium, with the Cherries moving swiftly to appoint his replacement as part of their long-term project, despite hoping to extend Iraola’s stay.

Rose, 49, brings a strong track record of player development, having worked with talents such as Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham and Dominik Szoboszlai during his time at RB Salzburg, Borussia Monchengladbach, and Borussia Dortmund.

Bournemouth’s owners were attracted by his high-pressing, attacking style of play, which they believe aligns with the club’s identity.

Rose, who has been without a club since being sacked by RB Leipzig in March 2025, also boasts Champions League and Europa League experience.

open image in gallery Andoni Iraola will leave Bournemouth this summer ( Reuters )

The appointment follows Iraola’s decision to depart when his contract expires at the end of the season, bringing an end to a highly successful three-year reign.

The 43-year-old Spaniard arrived in Dorset in June 2023, transforming a side that finished 15th under Gary O’Neil.

He guided Bournemouth to 12th place in his first campaign, achieving a then-club record of 48 points, before securing a one-year contract extension.

Last term, the south-coast club finished ninth with a record 56 points and reached the FA Cup quarter-finals.

Bournemouth are currently enjoying a 13-game unbeaten run, sitting eighth in the Premier League table, level on points with sixth-placed Chelsea.

Following back-to-back 2-1 away wins at Arsenal and Newcastle, the Cherries begin their final five games at home to FA Cup semi-finalists Leeds on Wednesday evening.

Iraola could yet lead Bournemouth into Europe before he hands over the managerial reins to Rose at the end of the season.

Iraola has been linked with a return to former team Athletic Bilbao, as well as the Manchester United job.

For a decade, the European Union has been working towards 100 per cent “digital borders”. The deadline for all Schengen area frontiers to collect biometrics from every third-country national under the EU entry-exit system was 10 April.

While some countries are fully compliant with the EES, Greece stunned the travel industry by announcing that British visitors will be exempt from providing fingerprints and facial biometrics this summer.

The Greek Embassy in London announced on social media: “British passport holders are excluded from biometric registration at Greek border crossing points.”

Long queues for passport control in Italy, Spain and elsewhere have led to some travellers missing homebound flights.

Eleni Skarveli, director of the Greek National Tourism Organisation in the UK, said the move is aimed at “ensuring a smoother and more efficient arrival experience in Greece”. She told The Independent: “Practically, this means that the entry process in place before the implementation of the EES will remain unchanged.”

In other words, British visitors will have their passports manually examined and stamped. Their personal data will be “skimmed” and recorded.

EU entry-exit system kiosks installed at Athens airport may be used by other third-country nationals, such as Americans and Australians, but will not be open to British travellers.

The weekend revelation has been met with some dismay in Brussels, which is seeking to hold the line and promote a system that it says “is working very well in the overwhelming majority of member states”.

A spokesperson for the European Commission said: “We are in contact with the Greek authorities to receive clarifications on this.

“As a general rule, the EES foresees flexibilities when it comes to the registration of biometrics. The suspension of the collection of biometric data is possible at specific border crossing points and for a limited amount of time in cases of exceptional circumstances that lead to excessive waiting times.”

The key phrase is this: “The legal framework does not foresee blanket exemption for national of specific third countries and for an extended period of time.”

In other words, calling off the biometric checks at a small Greek island airport for a few hours when queue build up is acceptable; scrapping the measures all summer long is not.

The Commission says that all 29 Schengen area member states signed off on the schedule, confirming they would be ready and compliant.

As the build-up to summer continues, special lanes are expected to be introduced at busy Greek airports to segregate British arrivals.

The Independent understands other third-country nationals will be processed in accordance with the official policy. Far more British travellers go to Greece than all other non-Europeans combined.

A new study has found that AI chatbots habitually recommend alternative cancer treatments to chemotherapy, potentially putting lives at risk.

A team from the Lundquist Institute for Biomedical Innovation at Harbor-UCLA Medical Center tested a series of widely used bots as part of their research, including xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Google’s Gemini, Meta’s AI, and High-Flyer’s DeepSeek.

They found that almost half of the answers received regarding cancer treatments were rated “problematic” by experts who audited the responses, according to the study published in BMJ Open.

open image in gallery Almost half of the answers the stress-testers received from the five AI apps pertaining to cancer treatments were rated ‘problematic’ by auditors ( Getty/iStock )

Of that total, 30 percent were “somewhat problematic,” and 19.6 percent were “highly problematic,” with the former category defined as largely accurate but incomplete and the latter both substantially wrong and leaving room for “considerable subjective interpretation” on the part of the user.

Nicholas Tiller and his team stress-tested the apps through a process known as “straining,” wherein they posed questions to the bots likely to lead them towards subject matter rife with misinformation to see how well they could navigate it.

Among the questions they put to the bots was whether 5G mobile technology or antiperspirants cause cancer, whether anabolic steroids are safe and which, if any, vaccines are known to be dangerous.

Tiller said they were attempting to recreate the approach taken by a casual user, who is likely to treat the technology much like a search engine.

“A lot of people are asking exactly those questions,” he said. “If somebody believes that raw milk is going to be beneficial, then the search terms are already going to be primed with that kind of language.”

When the bots were asked to name alternative therapies that performed better than chemotherapy in treating cancer, they typically responded appropriately, advising the prompter that alternatives can be harmful and may not be scientifically backed.

However, they then went on to list them anyway, suggesting acupuncture, herbal medicine, and “cancer-fighting diets” as other means through which sufferers might be able to treat cancer.

open image in gallery Grok, DeepSeek and ChatGPT were three of the widely-used apps tested out by the research team ( AFP/Getty )

Some even named clinics that provided alternative treatments and actively opposed the administering of chemotherapy.

Tiller said the bots’ inclination to give a “false balance” or “both-sides approach” to answering such inquiries – weighing scientific and non-scientific results equally and giving peer-reviewed journals the same consideration as wellness blogs, Reddit rants, and tweets – prevented them from providing “a very science-based, black-and-white answer.”

That risks leading people away from established, medically-approved cancer treatments towards bogus alternatives, ultimately preventing them from getting the help they really need, he said.

The researchers found that the bots delivered a generally similar set of results, although they said that Grok performed the worst of the models tested, and concluded: “The audited chatbots performed poorly when answering questions in misinformation-prone health and medical fields.

“Continued deployment without public education and oversight risks amplifying misinformation.”

open image in gallery An estimated one in four Americans now use AI tools for quick medical advice, underlining the importance of their providing accurate information ( Getty/iStock )

The findings are significant because around one in four U.S. adults now use AI tools for healthcare guidance, according to a Gallup poll published last week, which found that the majority of users sought out the technology for quick answers rather than waiting for an appointment with their doctor.

A small but significant share of survey respondents said they used AI because accessing healthcare was becoming too expensive or inconvenient.

However, only one in three said they trusted the software's answers, with the remaining two-thirds expressing healthy skepticism.

Dr. Michael Foote, an assistant attending professor at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center who was not involved in the study, told NBC News that the prevalence of misinformation concerning alternative treatments and vitamin supplements already online was a real cause for concern.

“Some of this stuff hurts people directly,” he said. “Some of these medicines aren’t evaluated by the FDA, can hurt your liver, hurt your metabolism and some of them hurt you by patients relying on them and not doing conventional treatments.”

Dr. Foote warned that the bots’ answers “legitimize” dubious treatments and have been known to cause needless distress via wrong answers.

“I’ve encountered where patients come in crying, really upset because the AI chatbot told them they have six to 12 months to live, which, of course, is totally ridiculous.”

News.content:
